rationale: Mixin APPLICATION vs INHERITANCE, discriminated by the SHAPE of the heritage expression: `Post extends Tagged(Timestamped)` CALLS a factory, so it is a `mixes_in` edge to the CALLEE `Tagged` AND an `extends` edge whose base name is also the callee — the javascript lane's measured convention, where 76 call-shaped heritage clauses give 76 `extends` and 83 `mixes_in`. `Plain extends Timestamped` names a type and is an `extends` edge only. THE FIXTURE FOUND A REAL DEFECT ON ITS FIRST RUN: the base name of a call-shaped heritage was the WHOLE CALL TEXT `Tagged(Timestamped)`, a target no symbol can own. Both directions are pinned, including that the ARGUMENT never becomes a target.

expectRelationships.note: the triple-slash reference directive is the one surface that emits part_of on this lane; the mutant that drops the whole type must fail HERE

forbidRelationships.note: THE DEFECT THIS FIXTURE CAUGHT: a call-shaped heritage published its base name as the whole call text, so the edge named `Tagged(Timestamped)` — a target that no symbol can own. The base name is the callee.
the ARGUMENT of the factory is not the mixin's target — the relation is to the callee
a plain type name in the heritage position is INHERITANCE, not an application; this is the negative half that makes the shape test real
